narrative:
The model determined that you have a 50% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability reached the threshold the bank uses to approve loans, your application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and the purpose of the loan. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative account, while 59% have no checking account at all. This status strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk.

The 12-month duration you requested worked in your favor. Approved applicants typically ask for almost 20 months, so your shorter term helped pull the prediction back toward approval. Unfortunately, this positive effect was not enough to overcome the other factors.

Your request for a new car also increased the risk score. While new-car loans are fairly common, the model sees them as carrying higher risk than loans for radio/TV or furniture, which dominate among approved applicants.

To improve your chances next time, bring your checking account balance above zero and keep it positive for several months before reapplying. Consider requesting a slightly longer repayment period if your budget allows, or explore whether a different purpose for the loan might be viewed more favorably. These steps should meaningfully improve how the model evaluates your application. (248 words)
